newsitem.title: USA: C.R. Bard wins FDA approval for new stent.
newsitem.headline: C.R. Bard wins FDA approval for new stent.

text.p: C.R. Bard Inc said on Monday that it has received FDA clearance to market the Memotherm Nitinol stent for use in treating biliary obstruction.
The device's design minimizes shortening of the stent upon deployment, the company said, making it easier to place.
And it added that the stent is made of Nitinol, giving it flexibility and strength.

"The Memotherm Nitinol Stent broadens Bard's U.S. offering in our oncological diagnosis and intervention product group," said chairman and chief executive officer, William Longfield. "Approximately 32,000 individuals will develop a biliary obstruction each year and many of these are appropriate candidates for the Memotherm Stent."
C.R. Bard Inc, headquartered in Murray Hill, N.J., is a multinational manufacturer and marketer of health care products.
